text.p: Pepsi-Gemex SA de CV said Monday its 50 percent-owned joint venture has acquired Embotelladora Agral Regiomontana SA de CV and its related companies, which constitute the Northeast Bottling Group.
Northeast Bottling, known as Agral, holds the Pepsi franchise for Monterrey and much of northeastern Mexico.
The joint venture is owned by Pepsi-Gemex and Pepsi-Cola Mexicana SA de CV.
Pepsi-Gemex said the joint venture acquired Agral using methods similar to those of a pre-packaged financial restructuring plan in the U.S.
It said more than 85 percent of the indebtedness of the Agral companies was acquired, at varying discounts, based upon the extent of security and guarantees for individual obligations.
An aggregate payment of $50 million including initial working capital, was provided by a newly formed joint venture company, Tenedora del Noreste SA de CV.
Under the terms of the joint venture, control over Noreste was granted to Pepsi-Gemex.
Pepsi-Gemex has an exclusive option to acquire Pepsi-Cola Mexicana's interest through 2002.
Operating control over the franchise has been granted to Pepsi-Gemex through 2002.
Pepsi-Gemex also acquired the exclusive option to acquire Pepsi-Cola Mexicana's interest in the joint venture though this period.
Pepsi-Gemex said the the 1,700 jobs that the bottling operation provides to the Monterrey area will be preserved.
